title: Finite discrete geometry of a zero-dimensional scheme
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a separated, locally finite type, quasi-compact morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], where $\dim |C|\le0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then $|C|$ is finite and discrete. Every $c\in|C|$ is closed [def-weil-closed-points], and the induced residue-field map $\kappa(f(c))\to\kappa(c)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is an isomorphism. Here $\operatorname{Spec}k$ denotes the affine spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Lemma Tag 00KH (Noetherian of dimension 0 = Artinian, finitely many maximal primes), Lemma Tag 00P4 (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-preserved-field-extension: dimension at a point is preserved by ground field extension); residue fields by the Nullstellensatz (Tag 00FV); fibres of a base change: literature/stacks-project/schemes.tex Lemma Tag 01JT (points of a fibre product)

proof.text: Use LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian, IsLocallyArtinian.of_topologicalKrullDim_le_zero, and QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace to make C Artinian. Its point set is finite and discrete by the Artinian instances.

Every singleton is closed in the discrete space. SpecMap_residueFieldIsoBase_inv identifies C.fromSpecResidueField(c) composed with f as Spec of an isomorphism. Apply the same identity to the identity of Spec k to make its fromSpecResidueField an isomorphism. The residue-field naturality identity and isIso_comp_right_iff then make Spec.map(f.residueFieldMap c) an isomorphism; reflection by Scheme.Spec and passage from the opposite category give the required IsIso.
